title: Can this win be real?
hook: A spectacular sales lift arrives with a duplicate-event bug.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: any result that looks too good is usually an error; walk through a surprising win and find the bug.

misconception: Treating twyman's law as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: any result that looks too good is usually an error; walk through a surprising win and find the bug.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Both versions truly have 1,000 visits and 100 sales. The variant logs each sale twice. After de-duplicating by sale ID, what sales lift remains?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-twyman-s-law/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Actual visits1000 and sales100 in both versions. Variant accidentally logs each sale twice: displayed200 and apparent+100%. De-duplicate event IDs to restore100; plot raw vs unique counts.

claims.text: A surprising result is a reason to test the measurement pipeline before inventing a product explanation. This example supplies the bug explicitly; it does not say that every large result is false or that de-duplication solves every logging problem.
